newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton closes barely up, dismisses USDA data.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton closes barely up, dismisses USDA data.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed slightly firmer in thin and technical trade, floor sources said.
The new-crop December contract settled 0.23 cent higher at 75.63 cents a lb. Spot July ended up 0.09 cent at 72.62 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.25 to 0.10 cent higher.

Traders attributed gains to speculative short-covering ahead of the July contract's expiry on Tuesday. The July/October spread should remain in the spotlight through the expiry, when the market is expected to turn its attention to the fundamental picture.
As of early Wednesday, open interest in July stood at 16,158 lots, down 1,635 lots from the previous session.
Ongoing cool and wet weather throughout the Delta is expected to give way to warmer conditions, providing better growing conditions for the cotton crop.

"The news is actually good," Weather Services Corp meteorologist Mike Palmerino, said. "Warmer and drier weather in the Delta and the Southeast should improve the crop, with temperatures reaching the low 90s (degrees Fahrenheit) through the early part of next week."
The improved forecast is likely to provide incentive for the December contract to move higher, said traders, pegging resistance at 75.60 cents, followed by 76.10 cents.
Earlier today, the U.S. Department of Agriculture reported new sales for the week ended June 12 at 80,900 480-lb bales in the 1996/97 crop, and at 67,700 bales in the new crop.
Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots compared with Wednesday's official 12,086 lots.
